source_text: Si enim Adam, ut dicitis, peccato naturali generavit omnes in condemnationem tantumque de suis visceribus in sobolem virus effudit, ut in natura hominis cuncta Dei instituta turbaret.
pass_a_gloss: For if Adam, as you say, by a natural sin generated all into condemnation and poured so much poison from his own inward parts into offspring that he disturbed all God's ordinances in the nature of a human being.

lemmas.lexica: LS generatio; Blaise vs imitatio in Rom 5:12
LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS institutum; Blaise God's ordinances of nature

pass_b_english: For if Adam, as you say, through natural sin begot everyone for condemnation and poured so much poison from his own body into his offspring that he disrupted every ordinance God had placed in human nature (compare Romans 5:18)— (Romans 5:18)

choices.why: Julian's target is Augustine's claim that sin is transmitted by begetting; keep generation vs imitation.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
